raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On a PD prefill worker under the overlap scheduler, `_send_kv_chunk` already hands a sender that declares `supports_host_tensor_indices` its KV page indices as a pinned host tensor plus a CUDA event, so the scheduler thread does not wait on the in-flight forward to send a chunk (#45492). The last chunk's state payloads were left out of that path: the sliding-window and full-KV state page indices still went through `kv_to_page_indices`, a `.cpu()` on the schedule stream. `_apply_war_barrier` fences that stream behind the running forward, so the copy returns only when that forward's reads are done, and the scheduler thread still blocked once per request, in `process_batch_result`, right before the hand-off to the transfer.

## Modifications

- `_send_kv_chunk` decides the host-tensor path once per call: a sender with `supports_host_tensor_indices`, outside the context-parallel transfers that filter indices on the host. The per-segment KV page indices use it as before.
- The last chunk's SWA-window and full-KV state page indices now take the same copy (`async_d2h` into pinned memory), returned as a NumPy view of the host tensor so the sender's consumers keep their types. The state rides the last segment's send, whose `indices_event` is recorded after these copies on the same stream; the Mooncake transfer worker already synchronizes that event before it reads the chunk, and on the scheduler thread the sender only takes their length.
- Senders without host-tensor support keep the synchronous read. The Mamba and DSA state payloads are unchanged; they do not go through `kv_to_page_indices`.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerics change: the same page indices reach the transfer, later. Ran the unit tests that drive `_send_kv_chunk` and the Mooncake chunk queue against this branch:

```
pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_minimax_m31_cache_transfer.py \
       test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_mooncake_transfer_batching.py \
       test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_fake_kv_sender.py
61 passed, 33 subtests passed
```

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci).
- [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation).
- [ ] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#accuracy-results).

+from sglang.srt.utils.common import async_d2h

     from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler import GenerationBatchResult, Scheduler
@@ -1579,6 +1580,26 @@ def _send_kv_chunk(
             )
             return
 
+        sender = req.disagg_kv_sender
+        # The schedule stream may wait on the in-flight forward. A sender that takes
+        # host-tensor indices waits on their copy's event itself, so the scheduler
+        # never blocks on these device reads.
+        host_indices = getattr(sender, "supports_host_tensor_indices", False) and not (
+            sender.kv_mgr.enable_all_cp_ranks_for_transfer
+            and not get_parallel().enable_dsa_cache_layer_split
+        )
+
+        def page_indices_of(kv_indices: torch.Tensor):
+            if not host_indices:
+                return kv_to_page_indices(kv_indices, page_size)
+            return async_d2h(kv_indices[::page_size] // page_size)
+
+        def state_page_indices(kv_indices: torch.Tensor) -> np.ndarray:
+            # State rides the last segment's send, whose indices_event is
+            # recorded behind this copy on the same stream.
+            page_indices = page_indices_of(kv_indices)
+            return page_indices.numpy() if host_indices else page_indices
+
         state_indices: Optional[List] = None
         if last_chunk:
             self.disagg_metadata_buffers.set_buf(req)
